t.6.15.1: Then from the midst of the ocean Sāgara himself rose up, like the sun rising from the great mountain Meru; the Ocean appeared together with serpents whose mouths were blazing.
t.6.15.2: He gleamed like polished lapis lazuli and was adorned with ornaments of jāmbūnada gold; he wore red garlands and garments, and his eyes were like lotus petals.
t.6.15.3: The mighty Ocean came forward and first greeted Rāghava, who stood with an arrow in his hand. Then, with joined palms, he spoke these words to him.
t.6.15.4: Earth, wind, space, the waters and fire, and Rāghava too, O gentle one, abide in their own nature, keeping to the eternal path.
t.6.15.5: This too is my very nature, that I am fathomless and cannot be crossed; to become fordable would be a perversion of my nature. This I declare to you.
t.6.15.6: Not out of desire, nor out of greed, nor out of fear, O son of a king, could I in any way make my waters, teeming with sharks and crocodiles, stand still.
t.6.15.7: I shall arrange it, O Rāma, and I shall bear it in such a way that the crocodiles will not strike for as long as the army is crossing.
t.6.15.8: O gentle one, this is Nala by name, the son of Viśvakarman; glorious, granted a boon by his father, he is the equal of Viśvakarman.
t.6.15.9: Let this monkey of great energy build a bridge upon me; I shall bear it up, for he is just like his father.
t.6.15.11: Relying on my father's power, I shall build a bridge across the vast abode of Varuṇa; the great ocean has spoken the truth.
t.6.15.10: Having spoken thus, the Ocean vanished. Then Nala, the mighty one, best of the vānaras, rose up and spoke these words to Rāma.
t.6.15.12: A boon was granted to my mother on Mount Mandara by Viśvakarman. I am his own son, born of his body, and I am equal to Viśvakarman.
t.6.15.13: Nor would I, unasked, proclaim my own virtues. Let the bulls among the monkeys build the bridge this very day, if they will.
t.6.15.14: Then, dismissed by Rāma, the leaders of the monkey troops, rejoicing, rushed in hundreds of thousands into the great forest on every side.
t.6.15.15: There those monkeys, mountain-like bulls among the hosts of tree-dwellers, broke the trees and dragged them to the ocean.
t.6.15.16: Those monkeys, with sāla trees and aśvakarṇa trees, with dhavas and bamboos, and with kuṭajas, arjunas, palmyras, tilakas and timiśas as well.
t.6.15.17: With bilva trees, saptaparṇa trees and flowering karṇikāra trees, with mango trees and aśoka trees, they filled up the ocean.
t.6.15.18: The best of the monkeys raised up trees, some with their roots and some without, as if lifting the banners of Indra, and those monkeys struck out with the trees.
t.6.15.19: Struck up suddenly by the mountains being hurled into it, the water rose up into the sky and then receded on every side.
t.6.15.20: In the midst of the ocean, lord of rivers and streams, Nala built a great bridge, ten yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long.
t.6.15.21: As rocks were being hurled and mountains were being thrown down there, a tumultuous sound then arose in that great ocean.
t.6.15.22: That bridge built by Nala across the ocean, the abode of makaras, shone beautiful and splendid, like the path of Svāti across the sky.
t.6.15.23: Then the gods together with the Gandharvas, and the Siddhas and the supreme seers.
t.6.15.24: The monkeys leapt about, bounding and roaring, and all beings beheld that bridge being built across the ocean, unimaginable, unbearable, wondrous and hair-raising.
t.6.15.25: Those thousands of crores of mighty monkeys, building a bridge across the sea, went to the far shore of the great ocean.
t.6.15.26: Broad, well constructed, splendid, with a fine surface and firmly compacted, that great causeway shone in the ocean like the parting line of hair on the head of a woman.
t.6.15.27: Then, on the far shore of the ocean, Vibhīṣaṇa, mace in hand, stood together with his ministers, ready to strike down the enemies.
t.6.15.28: At the head of that army went the glorious Rāma, the righteous-souled bowman, together with Lakṣmaṇa and accompanied by Sugrīva.
t.6.15.29: Some of the monkeys went along the middle, others along the sides; some fell into the water, others could not find the way; and some, taking to the sky, sped onward like Suparṇa birds.
t.6.15.30: With its mighty roar the fearsome army of monkeys, as it crossed over, drowned out the dreadful, towering roar of the ocean.
t.6.15.31: That army of monkeys, having crossed over by Nala's bridge, was encamped by the king on the shore, which abounded in roots, fruits and water.
t.6.15.32: Beholding that wondrous and difficult feat of the Rāghava, the gods, together with the Siddhas and Cāraṇas and accompanied by the great sages, approached Rāma and each anointed him separately with most auspicious waters.
t.6.15.33: "O god among men, conquer your enemies and rule the sea-girt earth for endless years!" With such varied and auspicious words they honored Rāma, who was revered by kings.
